question: Can we reuse code from a project we built before the event?
answer_text: Yes, you can generally reuse code from a project you built before the event, but it depends on the event’s rules. Some hackathons or competitions allow pre-existing code and libraries, while others require you to build everything during the event. Make sure to check the official guidelines, especially regarding code reuse, originality, and disclosure requirements. When in doubt, clearly mention which parts were developed before the event and which parts you created during it.

passages.text: Form a Team & Build: Create a working project from scratch on the day using open-source tools or open-weight AI models. Share Your Work: Push your project to a public GitHub repository under an open-source license. Demo Your Project: Present a quick 5-minute live demo of what your team built.

passages.text: Hacks do not have to be “innovative”. If somebody wants to work on a common idea, they should be allowed to do so and should be judged on the quality of their hack. These days it’s hard to find something that’s fully original and teams might not know an idea has been done before anyway. Teams can work on an idea that they have worked on before (as long as they do not re-use code or other project materials). Teams can use libraries, frameworks, or open-source code in their projects. Working on a project before the event and open-sourcing it for the sole purpose of using the code during the event is against the spirit of the rules and is not allowed. Teams must stop hacking once the time is up. However, teams are allowed to debug and make small fixes to their programs after time is up.
